bio_en: Poghos Papazian, called Yegho, was a native of Zmara who married around 1894; when an influential Turkish official plotted to abduct his wife he killed him and fled to Constantinople, working among bakers from his home town. There he killed the informer Father Mambre, pinning the ARF verdict to his cassock. Later, arrested after settling accounts with an anti-Armenian Tatar in the Caucasus, he was exiled to Siberia and Sakhalin, freed when the Japanese took Sakhalin in 1905, and made his way via Tiflis to Bulgaria, where he worked as a baker and cook at an ARF school until 1908. After the 1908 constitution he returned to Constantinople, later went to America, and in 1914 answered the party's call and returned; he appears in Murad's memoirs, and his grave is unknown.
